items.title: Job matching
items.goal: Every candidate gets a 0–100 score against a job, with matched, missing and uncertain skills each backed by the CV text they came from. Scoring ignores protected attributes, counts nationality and language only when the job requires them with a written reason, caps the score when a must-have is absent, and is keyed to the job version and model version so a stale score is never shown. The recruiter sees a ranked list they sort and filter; the AI never shortlists anyone.
prd: Job matching → Match output (decided): 0–100 score, skills matched/missing/uncertain with CV evidence, a ranked list the recruiter sorts and filters; the AI never shortlists, rejects or advances → decided
Job matching → requirement 1: nationality and language only with a written reason → decided
Job matching → requirement 2: scoring ignores name, photo, age, gender, race, religion, marital status → decided
Job matching → requirement 3: a missing must-have caps the score, for example at 50 → proposed
Job matching → requirement 4: the score shows the model version and date; changing the job recalculates all scores → proposed
Job matching → requirement 5: in the MVP all sample CVs are scored against every sample job → proposed
AI pipeline → Matching: filters first, then the top 50 by vector similarity per job, then a model call scores each one → suggested
exit: Redaction provably removes every protected attribute before any scoring call
A missing must-have caps the score, proven by tests at the cap boundary
Every stored score carries its job version and model version, and a stale score is never displayed
A recruiter can sort and filter the ranked list and add a candidate to the pipeline themselves
outOfScope: Any automatic shortlisting, rejection or advancement — the AI only suggests
Scoring on pregnancy, caregiving, disability or mental health: not in scope, and not to be added before the compliance review decides
Scoring candidates from external sources — a non-goal
Sending a shortlist to a client — a non-goal

items.title: CVs and jobs have multilingual embeddings
items.story: As a recruiter, I want an English job description to find a Chinese CV that fits, so that language is not an accidental filter on who I see.
ac: Given a CV in English or Simplified Chinese, when it is embedded, then a vector is stored with the embedding model's id.
Given a job version, when it is saved, then its embedding is created and stored the same way.
Given the embedding provider changes, when code is inspected, then no provider name appears outside the configured client.
prd: AI pipeline → Embeddings: a multilingual embedding model covering English and Simplified Chinese, stored with pgvector → suggested
Technical architecture → Search: pgvector for meaning-based search → proposed
Provider notes → embeddings may need a second provider → noted

items.title: Build the embedding service behind a provider-agnostic interface
items.what: Create one embedding service the whole app uses, with the provider behind an interface, storing the model id with every vector so a later model change is detectable. Test-first with a fake embedder.
scope: `src/server/ai/embeddings.ts`: embed text, embed a CV, embed a job version, all returning the model id
Failing tests first with a fake embedder: the model id is stored; a dimension mismatch against the stored schema is rejected; re-embedding the same text with the same model is skipped
Batched embedding for the seed's volume
No provider name outside the configured client module
exclusions: The pgvector index, which E03-S01-T03 created
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover model id storage, dimension mismatch and the re-embed skip
Every stored vector carries its embedding model id
Grep finds no provider name outside the client module
Unit tests make no network call

items.title: Each shortlisted-by-similarity candidate gets a fair, explained score
items.story: As a recruiter, I want a score I can justify to a client and to a candidate, so that I can say exactly which skills matched and where the evidence is.
ac: Given a CV containing a name, photo reference, age, gender, race, religion or marital status, when it is scored, then none of those reach the scoring call.
Given a job that does not require nationality or language with a written reason, when a candidate is scored, then neither affects the score.
Given a job requirement marked must-have that the candidate lacks, when the score is computed, then it is capped at the agreed value.
Given a stored score, when it is displayed, then it shows its model version and date, and a score from an older job version is never shown.
prd: Job matching → requirements 1, 2 → decided
Job matching → requirement 3: a missing must-have caps the score → proposed
Job matching → requirement 4: model version and date shown; changing the job recalculates → proposed
AI pipeline → Matching: filters first, then top 50 by vector similarity, then a model call per candidate → suggested
AI governance → requirement 1: every score shows the text it was based on → proposed

items.title: Write the match-scoring prompt and schema with rubric anchors
items.what: Write the schema and prompt that score one candidate against one job: a 0–100 score, matched, missing and uncertain skills, each with the CV text it came from, and rubric anchors so the number means the same thing every time.
scope: `src/ai/prompts/match-score/`: schema, prompt v1, fictional examples in English and Simplified Chinese
Rubric anchors describing what a score near 90, 70, 50 and 30 means
A rule in the prompt that only the job's stated requirements count, and that the model must not infer or use any protected attribute
Evidence required for every matched, missing and uncertain skill
A prompt version recorded on every run
exclusions: The redaction itself, which is enforced in code (T03)
The cap, which is applied in code (T03)
done: The schema requires evidence for every matched, missing and uncertain skill
Rubric anchors are stated for at least four score bands
The prompt forbids inferring or using protected attributes and forbids recommending a decision
Fictional English and Simplified Chinese examples are included

items.title: Build retrieval: hard filters then the top 50 by vector similarity
items.what: Before any scoring call, narrow the field: apply the job's hard filters, then take the top 50 candidates by vector similarity. This is what keeps the MVP's AI cost to about 1,000 scoring calls. Test-first.
scope: A retrieval function taking a job version and returning at most 50 candidate ids with their similarity
Failing tests first: hard filters exclude correctly; exactly 50 are returned when more qualify; fewer than 50 returns all; ties are broken deterministically
Protected attributes are never used as a filter unless the job requires nationality or language with a written reason
The similarity score retained so the ranked list can show why a candidate was considered
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover filter exclusion, the 50 cap, the under-50 case and deterministic tie-breaking
No protected attribute is used as a filter unless the job requires it with a written reason, proven by a test
Retrieval runs as one database query

items.title: Build the scoring service with protected-attribute redaction and the must-have cap
items.what: Score each retrieved candidate with one model call, but only after code has removed every protected attribute from what is sent, and apply the must-have cap in code afterwards. Fairness is enforced here, not in the prompt. Strictly test-first.
scope: Redaction in code before the call: name, photo reference, age, gender, race, religion, marital status always removed; nationality and language removed unless the job requires them with a written reason
Failing tests first, one per protected attribute, proving it does not reach the model payload

Failing tests first for the cap: a missing must-have caps the score at the agreed value; a score already below the cap is unchanged; multiple missing must-haves do not stack below the cap unless the spec says so
Evidence verification: a quote not present in the CV invalidates that skill claim
Every run written to `ai_runs` with model, version, prompt version, cost and duration
exclusions: Adding scoring on Workplace Fairness Act attributes not yet in scope
done: A test per protected attribute proves it is absent from the payload sent to the model
Failing-then-passing tests cover the cap at, above and below the boundary, and the multiple-must-have case
An invented evidence quote invalidates the skill claim rather than being stored
Every score row records the model version, prompt version and run id

items.title: Key scores to job version and model version and hide stale ones
items.what: Make the invariant real: a score belongs to a candidate, a job version and a model version, and the app never shows a score computed against a different job version or an older model. Test-first.
scope: A read path that resolves scores only for the job's current version and the current model version

Failing tests first: a score for an older job version is not returned; a score from an older model version is marked stale and not shown as current; a job saved with no scores yet returns an explicit not-yet-scored state rather than nothing
The model version recorded with each score and surfaced to the UI alongside the date
exclusions: Deleting old scores — history is kept
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the old-job-version, old-model-version and not-yet-scored cases
No read path can return a score whose job version differs from the job's current version
Every returned score carries its model version and computation date

items.title: Saving a job re-scores candidates in the background
items.story: As a recruiter, I want the job form to save straight away and the scores to catch up on their own, so that changing a requirement does not mean staring at a spinner.
ac: Given I save a job, when the response returns, then it returns without waiting for re-scoring.
Given re-scoring is running, when I open the job, then it tells me scores are being recalculated rather than showing stale ones as current.
Given a re-score run fails partway, when it is retried, then it resumes rather than starting from scratch.
prd: Job matching → requirement 4: changing the job recalculates all scores → proposed
Main flows → Saving a job: candidates are re-scored after the response is sent, using Next.js after(); progress is saved in a runs table so failed runs can be retried → suggested
Free-tier limits → Vercel Hobby cron runs once a day, so no frequent background jobs → decided

items.title: Re-score after the response with a retryable runs table
items.what: After a job save responds, re-score its candidates in the background using `after()`, recording progress in a runs table so a failed run can be retried from where it stopped rather than repeated in full.
scope: A re-score run row per job version: pending, running, failed, complete, with per-candidate progress
`after()` triggering the run from the save path so the response is not delayed

Failing tests first: the save responds before scoring completes; a failure marks the run failed with its position; a retry resumes from that position; two saves in quick succession do not run twice for the same version
A user-visible state on job detail while a run is in progress
exclusions: A cron job — Vercel Hobby runs cron once a day, so this is request-triggered
Queueing outside Supabase — job state stays in Supabase so CV text does not leave Singapore
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the non-blocking response, failure position, resumed retry and the duplicate-save case
Job detail shows that scores are being recalculated while a run is in progress
Run state lives in Supabase, not in an external queue

items.title: Recruiters review ranked matches and decide themselves
items.story: As a recruiter, I want a ranked list of candidates for a job with the reasons in front of me, so that I choose who to put forward and can explain why.
ac: Given a job with scores, when I open it, then candidates are ranked with their score, matched, missing and uncertain skills, and the CV text behind each.
Given the list, when I sort or filter it, then the ranking updates without re-running any AI call.
Given a candidate in the list, when I add them to the pipeline, then it is my action, and no candidate is pre-selected.
Given a score, when I look at it, then it is labelled as a suggestion and shows its model version and date.
prd: Job matching → Match output (decided): a ranked list the recruiter can sort and filter; the AI never shortlists, rejects or advances → decided
Job matching → requirement 4: the score shows the model version and date → proposed
UI design → Job detail: ranked matches with scores and reasons → decided
AI governance → the AI only suggests → decided

items.title: Build the ranked match list on job detail with add-to-pipeline
items.what: Build the ranked list from `design/specs/job-detail.md`: candidates ordered by score, with their matched, missing and uncertain skills and the CV text behind each, sortable and filterable, and an explicit add-to-pipeline action the recruiter takes.
scope: Server-rendered ranked list reading stored scores only — no AI call on page load
Sorting and filtering handled without re-scoring
`AiSuggestion` on every score with its model version and date, and `SourceQuote` on every skill claim
An add-to-pipeline action per candidate, with nothing pre-selected
Playwright coverage at both widths
exclusions: Bulk add, or any pre-selection of candidates
Sending a shortlist anywhere — a non-goal
done: Opening a job makes no AI call, proven by a test that fails on an unexpected model call
Every score shows its model version and date and is labelled as a suggestion
No candidate is selected by default and adding to the pipeline is always a recruiter action
Playwright passes at desktop and phone width with the shared assertions
